description: Start, talk to and remove child agents on your daemon. op add starts an existing definition def; op new writes a new definition at path (copy of from plus files) and starts it. A child does not inherit your brain or tools: give llm and tools. op say sends and returns; op ask waits for the answer; op rm removes; op ls shows the daemon table. Errors: ChildSlotMissing, ChildUnknown, ChildMissing, DefMissing, AddRejected. Details: memory node agents.

name.description: the child's name (new, add, say, ask, rm); letters, digits, _ and -

def.description: add: the existing definition folder, relative to your workspace or absolute; it must declare aos-agent in interfaces.json

path.description: new: where to write the new definition folder, relative to your workspace (it must stay inside it and must not exist yet)

from.description: new: the template folder to copy, relative to your workspace or absolute (e.g. the absolute path of proto8/templates/agent-fsm); leave it out to write the whole definition with files

files.description: new: files to write into the new definition, {relative path: full text}, e.g. {"system.txt": "You are a careful reviewer."} (agent-fsm keeps its system prompt in system.txt)

llm.description: new, add: brain settings, e.g. {"endpoint": "fake"} (agent-fsm) or {"model": "haiku"} (eca); new writes them into the definition's llm file, add into the child's own copy; default is what the definition says

tools.description: new, add: tools to give it (replaces one with the same name)

path.description: tool folder, relative to your workspace or absolute

tools_rm.description: new, add: names of tools to take away from it

ws.description: new, add: its workspace, relative to yours or absolute; created if missing; default is your own workspace

limits.description: new, add: resource limits for it, e.g. {"mem_mb": 512, "cpu_s": 600}; keys mem_mb, cpu_s, procs, file_mb, files (positive integers), user (string); default is what its definition declares

on_queued.description: new, add: fail on queue timeout (default), or ok to return queue position and start when a slot frees (op add: not with llm, tools or tools_rm)

ctl_timeout_s.description: new, add, rm: seconds to wait for the daemon to attach or remove the child; default 30, at most 1700

timeout_ticks.description: ask: positive integer ticks to wait, at most 9223372036854775777; the current clock/interval must also fit 30 extra ticks, otherwise ArgumentsBad before starting any subprocess; mutually exclusive with timeout_s; without AOS_TICK, one tick is AOS_TICK_INTERVAL milliseconds (default 1000)

timeout_s.description: ask: finite positive seconds to wait for the answer; default 600, at most 2147453; larger values give ArgumentsBad before starting any subprocess; mutually exclusive with timeout_ticks
